Alex: Heads-up — saw three OOMs on prod GPU pool during the midnight run. Traces point to batch formation pulling in requests with very large KV footprints. Need a quick triage before morning.
Priya: Uploaded a dashboard and sample logs: https://dash.redwood/prod/gpu-pool-2. Profiler shows KV memory spike at the batch assembly step — allocation jumps ~6GB -> 14GB per replica when a single long-kv request gets pulled in.
Dan: Reproduced locally with the seq-len/kv-size matrix. Kernel selection itself looks OK (int8 path), but eviction/soft-evict doesn't run early enough so the batch commits and then we OOM. Here's the memory timeline snippet I captured:
```
0s: batch start
20ms: assemble KV pointers
35ms: alloc +8GB for concatenated KV
40ms: eviction triggered (too late)
47ms: OOM on small pools
```
Mei: Short-term mitigation idea: admission rule that checks sum(kv_bytes in queue) + estimated_kv_of_batch > kv_capacity * 0.85 -> reject or defer. Bias admission against long-horizon KV (requests with large kv_bytes). :thinking_face:
Alex: Also noticed this correlates with the sparse-batcher change from last week (commit abc123) — window broadened which increased chance of mixing heavy KV requests into single batch. Could be both admission + window tuning needed.
Priya: I'll roll a canary that reduces batch window and also add a `kv_margin` config (default 0.1) to reserve headroom for eviction overhead. Config example: `kv_margin: 0.1` meaning we target 90% of reported KV capacity for admission decisions.
Dan: We should factor kernel-selection cost into batch scoring too. If combining two reqs would flip kernel path to a slower GEMM/large-tensor path, deprioritize that combo. Pseudocode for admission: 
```
function admit_batch(queue, kv_capacity, kv_margin):
  est_kv = sum(estimate_kv(req) for req in batch_candidates)
  if est_kv + current_kv_usage > kv_capacity * (1 - kv_margin):
    return DEFER
  if kernel_cost_estimate(batch_candidates) > latency_budget:
    deprioritize
  return ADMIT
```
Quick profiling command I used: `rb_profile --trace kv_alloc --since 1h` — shows the abrupt allocs during assembly.
Mei: Instead of flat rejects, can we funnel long-KV requests into a "slow-lane" queue with its own token budget and capped concurrent slots? That would avoid head-of-queue starvation while keeping critical SLO traffic flowing.
Alex: Proposed plan: 1) deploy kv_margin=0.1 to canary on pool-gpu-2, 2) add admission rule to batcher to check est_kv vs capacity, 3) reduce sparse-batcher window on canary, 4) monitor kernel-selection histograms and latency SLOs, 5) rollback if we see SLO break or no improvement, 6) postmortem if OOMs persist. I'll open the PR for the admission rule now.
Priya: I'll capture perf snapshots and kernel-selection histograms before/after canary and post results in #eng-runtime tomorrow morning. Also will tag the commit that introduced the batching window change for close inspection.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary started for kv_margin=0.1 on pool-gpu-2 at 1999999460
Dan: Thanks, will keep an eye on logs and run additional local reproductions. :thumbsup:
